from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.add(pencil_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.place_at_grid(water_label, 'D3')

        pencil_submerged = Line(start=UP*1, end=DOWN*2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=8)

        self.play(Transform(pencil, pencil_submerged))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00BFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(bend_highlight, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(refraction_text, 'B4')
        self.play(Create(bend_highlight), FadeIn(refraction_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Snell’s Law calculates the bending angle.",
            "It uses indices and sine values.",
            "The normal line is our reference.",
            "Compare the incident and refractive angles.",
            "Geometry predicts the path of light."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Snell’s Law: The Mathematical Geometry", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw two media layers
        air = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color="#F0F8FF", stroke_width=0)
        water = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color="#00BFFF", stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(air, "A1", "C6")
        self.place_in_area(water, "D1", "F6")
        self.play(FadeIn(air), FadeIn(water))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#F0F8FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw normal line
        normal = DashedLine(start=np.array([4.5, 2.5, 0]), end=np.array([4.5, -2.5, 0]), color="#808080")
        self.play(Create(normal))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#808080")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Incident ray
        incident_ray = Line(start=np.array([2.5, 1.5, 0]), end=np.array([4.5, 0, 0]), color="#FFD700", stroke_width=4)
        theta1_label = MathTex(r"\theta_1", color="#FFD700").next_to(incident_ray.get_end(), UP+LEFT, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(incident_ray), Write(theta1_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Refracted ray
        refracted_ray = Line(start=np.array([4.5, 0, 0]), end=np.array([6.0, -1.2, 0]), color="#32CD32", stroke_width=4)
        theta2_label = MathTex(r"\theta_2", color="#32CD32").next_to(refracted_ray.get_end(), DOWN+RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(refracted_ray), Write(theta2_label))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#32CD32")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Equation
        equation = MathTex(r"n_1 \sin(\theta_1) = n_2 \sin(\theta_2)", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "A3")
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Moving to denser media, light bends inward.",
            "Moving to lighter media, light bends outward.",
            "Always measure angles from the normal line."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Direction: Toward or Away from Normal", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visuals
        normal1 = DashedLine(UP*1.5, DOWN*1.5, color=GREY).shift(RIGHT*3)
        interface1 = Line(LEFT*1.5, RIGHT*1.5, color=WHITE).rotate(PI/2).shift(RIGHT*3)
        
        # Refraction 1: Air to Glass
        ray_in1 = Line(LEFT*1.5, ORIGIN, color=YELLOW)
        ray_out1 = Line(ORIGIN, DOWN*1, color=YELLOW).rotate(-0.3, about_point=ORIGIN)
        ray1 = VGroup(ray_in1, ray_out1).shift(RIGHT*3)
        
        # Refraction 2: Glass to Air
        normal2 = DashedLine(UP*1.5, DOWN*1.5, color=GREY).shift(RIGHT*5)
        interface2 = Line(LEFT*1.5, RIGHT*1.5, color=WHITE).rotate(PI/2).shift(RIGHT*5)
        ray_in2 = Line(UP*1, ORIGIN, color=YELLOW).rotate(0.3, about_point=ORIGIN).shift(RIGHT*5 + DOWN*0.5)
        ray_out2 = Line(ORIGIN, DOWN*1.5, color=YELLOW).rotate(0.6, about_point=ORIGIN).shift(RIGHT*5 + DOWN*0.5)
        ray2 = VGroup(ray_in2, ray_out2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(normal1), Create(interface1), Create(ray1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(Create(normal2), Create(interface2), Create(ray2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        angle_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=PI/2, angle=0.5, color="#FF4500")
        angle_arc.move_to(normal1.get_center() + RIGHT*0.2 + DOWN*0.2)
        self.play(Create(angle_arc))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Archer Fish", [
            "The archer fish hunts insects above.",
            "Refraction shifts the bug’s apparent position.",
            "The fish adjusts its aim to strike."
        ])
        
        water_surface = Line(start=self.grid["C1"] + LEFT*1, end=self.grid["C6"] + RIGHT*1, color=BLUE)
        water_text = Text("Water", font_size=16, color=BLUE).next_to(water_surface, DOWN)
        
        archer_fish = Dot(color="#00BFFF", radius=0.2)
        fish_label = Text("Archer Fish", font_size=16, color="#00BFFF").next_to(archer_fish, DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(archer_fish, "E3")
        self.add(fish_label)
        
        bug = Dot(color="#FFFFFF", radius=0.1)
        bug_label = Text("Bug (True)", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(bug, UP)
        self.place_at_grid(bug, "A4")
        self.add(bug_label)
        
        apparent_bug = Dot(color="#FFD700", radius=0.1)
        apparent_label = Text("Bug (Apparent)", font_size=16, color="#FFD700").next_to(apparent_bug, UP)
        self.place_at_grid(apparent_bug, "A2")
        self.add(apparent_label)
        
        # Light ray
        ray1 = Line(bug.get_center(), self.grid["C4"], color=WHITE)
        ray2 = Line(self.grid["C4"], archer_fish.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        illusion_ray = DashedLine(apparent_bug.get_center(), self.grid["C4"], color="#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(water_surface, water_text), FadeIn(archer_fish), FadeIn(fish_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00BFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(bug, bug_label), FadeIn(apparent_bug, apparent_label), Create(ray1), Create(ray2), Create(illusion_ray))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        aim_line = Line(archer_fish.get_center(), self.grid["C2"], color=RED, stroke_width=2)
        self.play(Create(aim_line))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Physics of Refraction: Why Light Bends

sections.title: The Hook: The Broken Pencil Illusion
sections.content: Introduce the phenomenon using a visual contrast: a pencil placed in a half-filled water glass appears 'broken' at the surface. Briefly establish that light travels in straight lines in a vacuum but changes behavior when entering denser matter.
sections.example: An animation showing a pencil entering water and the light rays 'kinking' at the air-water interface.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Speed of Light in Media
sections.content: Define the refractive index (n) as a ratio: n = c/v. Explain that light slows down in denser media (like glass or water) compared to a vacuum. Use the analogy of a marching band moving from pavement onto thick mud.
sections.example: A row of marchers represented by a line of light waves; as the front wheels (or marchers) hit the mud, they slow down, causing the entire line to pivot/turn.

sections.title: Snell’s Law: The Mathematical Geometry
sections.content: Introduce Snell’s Law: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2). Use a clear graphic showing the 'Normal' line perpendicular to the surface. Focus on the relationship between the angle of incidence and the angle of refraction.
sections.example: An interactive diagram where dragging the incident light beam dynamically updates the angles and the sine values in real-time.

sections.title: Visualizing Direction: Toward or Away from Normal
sections.content: Establish the rule: When moving from low-density (fast) to high-density (slow), light bends toward the normal. Moving from high to low, it bends away. Connect this to the 'marching band' analogy.
sections.example: Split-screen animation: One side showing air-to-glass (bending inward), the other showing glass-to-air (bending outward).

sections.title: Application: The Archer Fish
sections.content: Apply the concept to a real-world predator: The Archer Fish. It must compensate for light refraction to accurately spit water at insects above the surface. Summarize the lesson by noting that our eyes must account for this 'virtual image' shift.
sections.example: An animation of an Archer Fish looking up; show the 'apparent' position of the bug vs. its 'true' position, and the adjustment the fish makes to strike.
